propositions.text: The claimants seek protection in Canada under sections 96 and 97(1) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The claimants, XXXX XXXX, (principal claimant), XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, (the minor claimants), seek protection in Canada pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimants seek protection in Canada under sections 96 and 97(1) of IRPA, as stated by the applicant.

propositions.text: This is a hearing de novo of their claims, heard jointly under Rule 55(1) and the principal claimant is representative for the minors under IRPA section 167(2).
propositions.quote: This is a hearing de novo of their claims, which, pursuant to Rule 55(1) of the Refugee Protection Division Rules, were heard jointly. Also, pursuant to IRPA section 167(2), the principal claimant was designated the representative for the other three claimants, who are all minors.

paragraphs.summary: The court states this is a de novo joint hearing with the principal claimant as representative for the minors under IRPA section 167(2).

propositions.text: At hearing scheduling, the principal claimant was detained; the Minister was alerted to a possible exclusion issue but did not participate.
propositions.quote: At the time the hearing was scheduled, XXXX XXXX was detained at the Roy McMurty Youth Centre in Brampton. While the Division alerted the Minister to a possible exclusion issue arising from his detention, the Minister did not participate in the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the principal claimant was detained and the Minister was alerted but did not participate in the hearing.

propositions.text: The claims were originally joined with the principal claimant's husband's claim, which was disjoined and heard separately with a negative decision.
propositions.quote: Originally, these claims were joined with that of XXXX XXXX, the husband of the principal claimant. XXXX XXXX claim was disjoined at the hearing of January 31, 2012.

propositions.text: The principal claimant was designated representative of the minors at the January 31, 2012 hearing.
propositions.quote: It was at this hearing that the principal claimant was designated the representative of the minor claimants.

propositions.text: The husband's claim was refused judicial review by Federal Court and he has returned to Hungary.
propositions.quote: On April 26, 2012, the Federal Court refused his application for leave to have the Board's decision judicially reviewed. The principal claimant's husband has since returned to Hungary.

propositions.text: The minor claimants rely in part on the husband's narrative, as amended.
propositions.quote: all of the claimants rely, in part, on his narrative, as amended.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the claims were originally joined with the husband's, who was disjoined and refused judicial review; the principal claimant was designated representative for minors.

propositions.text: The principal claimant married XXXX XXXX in 2007.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant married XXXX XXXX in 2007.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the principal claimant married XXXX XXXX in 2007.

propositions.text: The principal claimant's husband described discriminatory incidents including attacks and threats against the family in Hungary.
propositions.quote: He described several discriminatory incidents, including an attack during which he was beaten with a baseball bat. His right shoulder was dislocated. In a second attack, he, the principal claimant and his "grandson" were attacked and he, XXXX XXXX, was beaten.

propositions.text: He described being refused promised employment and an incident on a streetcar where guardsmen spat on their daughter and beat them, threatening to kill if reported.
propositions.quote: In his amendment to the PIF, the principal claimant's husband described being refused promised employment at a bakery, when he turned up to sign the contract. He also described an incident on a streetcar during which three "guardsmen" spit on their daughter. When the family got off the streetcar, the guardsmen followed them. They beat them, and threatened to kill them were they to report the incident to the police.

paragraphs.summary: The husband's narrative describes discriminatory attacks, refused employment, and a violent streetcar incident with threats.

propositions.text: The principal claimant amended the narrative to say her husband was removed from Canada, lives in a shelter in Budapest, and faces racism and poor living conditions.
propositions.quote: In her amendment, she added that her spouse was removed from Canada following his failed claim, and that he now lives in a shelter in Budapest. She stated that he is forced to live in a shelter because, being Roma, he is unable to find work, and so is unable to find shelter of his own.

propositions.text: Their home is uninhabitable and the husband was attacked by racists, suffering a cut finger; police are known not to respond well to Roma complaints.
propositions.quote: Their own home in XXXX is not in a habitable condition, and the principal claimant's husband does not have the money either to repair or to rebuild it. He has been attacked by racists at least once, and suffered a cut finger during the incident. The principal claimant did not know if her husband had filed a police report regarding the incident, but noted that the Federal Court has recognised that the police are known not to respond well to complaints by Roma persons.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant amended the narrative describing her husband's removal, poor living conditions, racist attack, and police indifference to Roma complaints.

propositions.text: The principal claimant claimed she could not register their youngest child in daycare due to lack of residency document from landlord in Budapest.
propositions.quote: Also, in her amendment, the principal claimant claimed that when the family lived in Budapest, she was not able to register their youngest child in daycare because the landlord would not give them the document they needed to establish that they were residents of Budapest.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant claims inability to register youngest child in daycare due to landlord withholding residency document.

propositions.text: The principal claimant alleged returning to Hungary would harm minors' education and prospects, and her son has been negatively affected by father's absence.
propositions.quote: She alleged they would be put back to the grades they were in when they left Hungary, and their education would be adversely affected. The principal claimant also stated, that her son XXXX has been negatively affected by his father's absence. His conduct has attracted the involvement of police and the Children's Aid Society. She claimed that all of the minors would have better prospects for life in Canada than they would in Hungary.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant alleges return to Hungary would harm minors' education and prospects; son's conduct worsened by father's absence.

propositions.text: The determinative issues are credibility and state protection.
propositions.quote: The determinative issues in the claim are credibility and state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies credibility and state protection as the determinative issues.

propositions.text: A claimant's sworn testimony creates a rebuttable presumption of truthfulness unless valid reason to doubt exists.
propositions.quote: the panel is aware of the principle that when a claimant swears to the truth of certain statements, this creates a presumption that they are true, unless there is valid reason to doubt their truthfulness.

propositions.text: The principal claimant provided oral testimony but was found generally lacking credibility unless responding to leading questions.
propositions.quote: Overall, the panel found that she lacked credibility; unless she was responding to a leading question, her responses tended to be general.

paragraphs.summary: The court states sworn testimony creates a presumption of truthfulness but finds the principal claimant generally lacking credibility.

propositions.text: The previous hearing found the family is Roma ethnicity, which the panel accepts.
propositions.quote: The previous hearing of the claim found that the principal claimant had established the Roma ethnicity of the family, and the panel accepts that finding.

propositions.text: The panel had concerns about the principal claimant's testimony regarding her Roma ethnicity, especially her speech and mannerisms.
propositions.quote: However, the panel had concerns about aspects of her testimony regarding that ethnicity. The claimant's mother is white; her father was Roma. She testified that in Hungary, she is readily recognised as Roma by her manner of dress, speech and expression.

propositions.text: Interpreter said principal claimant used same Hungarian words but grammar made understanding difficult.
propositions.quote: To test this assertion, the panel asked the interpreter whether he perceived any differences in the principal claimant's speech. He responded that she used the same Hungarian words, but that he had some difficulty understanding her because of her grammar.

paragraphs.summary: The panel accepts Roma ethnicity but doubts the principal claimant's testimony about her Roma mannerisms and speech, based on interpreter's input.

propositions.text: Interpreter observed no difference in pronunciation or speech pattern of principal claimant.
propositions.quote: Counsel for the claimant asked the interpreter whether he had observed any differences in her pronunciation and speech pattern, to which the interpreter responded, there were none.

propositions.text: The panel is not persuaded that the principal claimant's speech was typically Roma given her mixed parentage and upbringing.
propositions.quote: For its part, the panel is not persuaded by the principal claimant's assertions that the way she spoke and use of language was typically Roma. Given that her mother is a white Hungarian, and also given that she was raised by her mother, the panel finds that it was equally likely that the principal claimant would speak like a white Hungarian.

propositions.text: The panel infers the principal claimant exaggerated her claims, indicating willingness to mislead the panel.
propositions.quote: The panel infers, that her claims were no more than exaggerations, and while not definitive of her credibility, were indicative of her willingness to mislead the panel.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no speech difference, doubts typical Roma speech claim, and infers exaggeration indicating willingness to mislead.

propositions.text: The principal claimant said they left Hungary due to humiliation, discrimination, unemployment and oppression because of Roma ethnicity.
propositions.quote: The panel asked the principal claimant why the family came to Canada. She responded, that they left Hungary because they were humiliated, given scant respect, unemployed and oppressed because of their Roma ethnicity.

propositions.text: She claimed racism and discrimination limited her formal education; she left school after Grade 8 due to bullying and lack of moral strength.
propositions.quote: She described some of the experiences that led to the decision to leave. For herself, she claimed that racism and discrimination led to her having limited formal education. She left school at the end of Grade 8 because of bullying, and a lack of "moral strength to continue."

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant said they left Hungary due to discrimination and she left school after Grade 8 due to bullying and lack of moral strength.

propositions.text: The panel finds valid reason to doubt and reject the principal claimant's stated reason for leaving school based on timing and pregnancy.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that there was valid reason to doubt, and to reject, the principal claimant's stated reason for leaving school.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds valid reason to doubt and reject the principal claimant's reason for leaving school.

propositions.text: At POE, the principal claimant stated fear of Hungarian Guard and described being insulted and spat on during bus ride.
propositions.quote: At the Port of Entry (POE), the principal claimant stated that she was afraid of the Hungarian Guard. She went on to state, that she was seeking Canada's protection "because we are Roma we are outcasted [sic]. Our lifeline or opportunities are totally cut off from us. When we were on the bus my child was insulted and spat on."

propositions.text: The husband's amended narrative added attackers followed and beat the family; the principal claimant testified attackers demanded her from husband.
propositions.quote: The amended narrative filed by her husband added, that the attackers had followed the family and beat them. In testimony, the principal claimant added, that the attackers demanded that her husband "give her to them".

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant stated fear of Hungarian Guard and described attacks; husband added attackers followed and beat them, attackers demanded her.

propositions.text: The panel is not persuaded the attackers demanded the husband give the principal claimant to them; this is likely an exaggeration.
propositions.quote: it is not persuaded of the truth of the whole of her statement. Specifically, the panel is not persuaded that the black uniformed men she described had demanded that her husband give her to them as she claimed.

propositions.text: The panel finds it unlikely the principal claimant could have been led away unwillingly in broad daylight if the demand was true.
propositions.quote: The incident allegedly took place in broad daylight, and the panel is not persuaded that, in the unlikely event that her husband had acceded to the request, the principal claimant could have been led away unwillingly.

propositions.text: The panel views this as another exaggeration by the principal claimant.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the view that this is another instance where she has exaggerated her experiences.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claim attackers demanded the husband give the principal claimant to them is not credible and likely exaggerated.

propositions.text: Board can reject credibility based on implausibilities if reasons are clear and inferences reasonable, citing Lubana and other cases.
propositions.quote: Normally, the Board is entitled to conclude that an applicant is not credible because of implausibilities in his or her evidence as long as its inferences are not unreasonable and its reasons are set out in "clear and unmistakable terms"

propositions.text: Board may reject uncontradicted evidence inconsistent with probabilities or with inconsistencies, citing cases.
propositions.quote: The Board may reject uncontradicted evidence if it is not consistent with the probabilities affecting the case as a whole, or where inconsistencies are found in the evidence

paragraphs.summary: The court cites case law allowing rejection of credibility based on implausibilities and inconsistencies if reasons are clear and inferences reasonable.

propositions.text: Following Martineau J., the panel rejects the principal claimant's evidence that the Hungarian Guard demanded her from her husband.
propositions.quote: Following the dicta of Martineau, J., the panel rejects the uncontradicted evidence of the principal claimant, that, the Hungarian Guard demanded that her husband give her to them during the alleged incident on the street car.

propositions.text: The panel finds such an incident would likely have been included in the husband's amended narrative if true.
propositions.quote: The panel further finds that, if true, this is the type of incident that the principal claimant's husband would likely have included in the amendment to this narrative.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claim attackers demanded the principal claimant and finds such an incident would likely have been included in the husband's narrative.

propositions.text: There is valid reason to question the principal claimant's account of police presence and inaction during the streetcar incident due to inconsistencies.
propositions.quote: there was additional valid reason to question the credibility of the principal claimant's account of the street car incident, with respect to the involvement of the police.

propositions.text: The principal claimant alleged police were present but treated them as perpetrators and yelled at them to go away.
propositions.quote: In response to her counsel, the principal claimant alleged that the police were present during the incident, but took no action to interfere. Instead, the police treated them as if they were the perpetrators, and not the victims. In her words, "they [the police] started to yell at us to go away".

propositions.text: The police presence and inaction was not mentioned in earlier narratives or at POE, and the principal claimant's testimony was internally inconsistent about filing a police report.
propositions.quote: That the police were present, but unhelpful, was not mentioned in either amendment to the narrative or at the POE. In fact, the principal claimant's testimony was itself internally inconsistent, as she initially testified that she did not file a police report about the incident because she did not know the names of their attackers, and could not file a report.

propositions.text: This inconsistency adds to the general untrustworthiness of the principal claimant's evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that this inconsistency adds to the general untrustworthiness of the principal claimant's evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds inconsistencies in the principal claimant's account of police presence and inaction, adding to her general untrustworthiness.

propositions.text: Minor claimants are important factors in the hearing and would face marginalization and ostracism if returned
propositions.quote: Counsel for the claimants submitted, that the minor claimants were important factors in the hearing. The panel concurs. On their behalves, the principal claimant submitted that, if returned, they would have experiences similar to hers, that is, they would be marginalised and ostracised.

propositions.text: Son, XXXX Jr., was locked in a classroom and this affected his school attendance in Toronto
propositions.quote: She claims that her son, XXXX Jr., already had one such experience where he was locked in a classroom instead of being allowed out to socialise with his classmates. In testimony, she blamed this experience for, at least in part, being responsible for his later reluctance to attend school here in Toronto.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues minor claimants would face marginalization if returned; son locked in classroom affected school attendance, court concurs on importance.

propositions.text: XXXX Jr. attended school briefly but refused to enter classroom and refused psychological counselling
propositions.quote: He appeared to have attended school for one term (semester) before he was brought to Canada. It was the principal claimant's evidence that XXXX Jr. last attended school in September 2016. She testified that for about three months he would go to school, but would not enter the classroom. He walked the hallways; he told her that he quite simply could not enter the classroom. Psychological counselling was recommended; but XXXX Jr. refused to attend.

propositions.text: XXXX Jr. fell in with bad company and was adversely affected by father's absence
propositions.quote: When questioned by her counsel, the principal claimant testified that XXXX Jr. had fallen in with "bad company." After being prompted further, she stated that he was adversely affected by his father's absence.

propositions.text: Principal claimant said they would see a psychologist but no objective evidence was provided
propositions.quote: She testified that "we are going to see a psychologist", but there was no objective evidence in the form or ether an appointment schedule, or report, put before the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant testifies XXXX Jr. refused classroom and counselling, fell in with bad company, affected by father's absence; no objective evidence of psychologist visits.

propositions.text: Multiple factors likely caused XXXX Jr.'s delinquency affecting academic achievement
propositions.quote: The panel accepts that a mix of factors likely affected and accounts for XXXX Jr.'s delinquency, and that this delinquency has affected his academic achievement.

propositions.text: Not persuaded XXXX Jr. would be placed in Grade 1 or reform school if returned to Hungary
propositions.quote: However, the panel is not persuaded, that upon return to Hungary, a fifteen to sixteen year old XXXX Jr. would be placed with children in Grade 1. Nor is the panel persuaded that he would be placed in a boarding (reform) school, as claimed.

propositions.text: XXXX Jr. appears to have abandoned schooling in Toronto and unlikely to resume in Hungary
propositions.quote: As it is, he appears to have abandoned schooling here in Toronto, and the panel is not persuaded that he would resume schooling in Hungary, all things being equal.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds multiple factors caused XXXX Jr.'s delinquency; not persuaded he would be placed in Grade 1 or reform school in Hungary; unlikely to resume schooling.

propositions.text: Accepts some dislocation for XXXX and XXXX due to possible inability to read/write Hungarian
propositions.quote: With respect to XXXX and XXXX, the panel accepts that they will experience some dislocation as they may, or may not, be able to read or write Hungarian.

propositions.text: Dislocation for XXXX would be similar to her initial experience in Canadian school system
propositions.quote: However, so far as XXXX is concerned that dislocation would be no different from her experience when she was first brought to Canada, and placed in the school system here.

propositions.text: No objective evidence that children would be placed in Grade 1 as asserted
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the principal claimant has not put any objective evidence before the panel to establish that the children would be put in Grade 1 as she asserted.

propositions.text: Testimony that children would be placed in Grade 1 is speculative and insufficiently credible
propositions.quote: The panel finds her testimony, that she was told this by persons who had returned to Hungary, speculative at best. Therefore, without more, the panel finds that there is insufficient credible evidence to persuade it that this would be the case.

paragraphs.summary: Court accepts some dislocation for children but finds no credible evidence they would be placed in Grade 1; dislocation similar to prior experience for one child.

propositions.text: Hungarian government centralized education responsibility to improve outcomes
propositions.quote: With respect to education, the panel notes to address the inequity. The Hungarian central government has taken the responsibility for education away from the municipal levels, and attributed it to the government, thus the centralization would lead to better outcome.

propositions.text: New school inspectorate system started operating in 2015
propositions.quote: A new school inspectorate system has also been set up and started to operate in 2015.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes Hungarian government centralized education and started new inspectorate system in 2015 to improve outcomes.

propositions.text: Government made significant efforts and EU co-funded programs to enforce equal educational opportunities
propositions.quote: significant governmental efforts have been made in recent years for the increased enforcement of equal opportunities in education. In addition to local programmes, programmes co-funded by the European Union...have been available in the magnitude of tens of billions of forints.

propositions.text: Integrated education widespread but drop-out rates and study results for disadvantaged students have not improved significantly
propositions.quote: While integrated education is largely wide-spread on an institutional level, drop-out rates and the study results of students with multiple disadvantages have yet to improve significantly.

propositions.text: Extracurricular learning centres assist disadvantaged children but sustainability and funding remain issues
propositions.quote: The extracurricular learning centres are a form of education opted for by children and their parents out of their own free will...As part of the programme, 60 alternative learning facility projects were financed in total. However, the sustainability of extra-curricular learning centres and the need for the streamlining of parallel institution development and funding forms are issues yet to be resolved.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes government and EU efforts to improve educational equality; integrated education widespread but challenges remain with drop-outs and funding.

propositions.text: Acknowledges discrimination against Roma children in Hungary's education system
propositions.quote: I acknowledge that the educational system in Hungary is not without discrimination towards Roma children, and that the EU has taken steps against it with respect to improvements in this area.

propositions.text: Hungarian Supreme Court ruled unlawful segregation of Romani children; European Commission launched infringement proceedings
propositions.quote: The ERRC also reports that between 2011 and 2016, the Hungarian Supreme Court ruled that Romani children were being unlawfully segregated in five cases...European Commission launched infringement proceedings against Hungary due to discrimination of Roma in Hungary's school system...

propositions.text: Kindergarten mandatory from age 3 but insufficient spaces for Roma children in segregated areas
propositions.quote: Sources indicate that in Hungary, it is mandatory for all children to start kindergarten from age 3...However, the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights notes that there are not enough kindergarten spaces for Roma children in segregated areas.

paragraphs.summary: Court acknowledges discrimination against Roma children; courts ruled unlawful segregation; EU infringement proceedings; kindergarten mandatory but insufficient spaces.

propositions.text: Hungary adopted EU Roma Integration Framework and developed National Social Inclusion Strategy
propositions.quote: The EU Roma Integration Framework was adopted under the Hungarian Presidency of the EU in the first half of 2011. Hungary was the first to develop its National Social Inclusion Strategy according to the EU framework.

propositions.text: Government aims for medium-term social and labour market integration of Roma and poor over 10 years
propositions.quote: According to Government declarations, ...in alignment with the EU framework of National Roma Integration Strategies up to 2020, the Government aims to determine the medium-term challenges and targets of the social and labour market integration of those living in poverty, including the Roma, as well as the necessary interventions, over a period of 10 years.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes Hungary adopted EU Roma Integration Framework and aims for 10-year social and labour market integration strategy for Roma.

propositions.text: Public Education Act 2007 made school enrolment stricter to reduce segregation and prioritize disadvantaged students
propositions.quote: Article 66 of the Public Education Act made the regulations concerning the enrolment of children in public schools stricter from January 1, 2007...schools must admit disadvantaged students first...percentage of multiply disadvantaged children within each school district must not be more than 15 percent higher or lower than the ratio...

propositions.text: Church-maintained schools required to enroll local children with priority to disadvantaged; central government took over schools from municipalities
propositions.quote: Other changes made it mandatory for schools and kindergartens maintained by churches and other institutions to enrol children who reside within the settlement...schools were taken by the central government from the municipalities.

propositions.text: Education Authority monitors enrolment compliance but rarely uses sanctioning power
propositions.quote: The 2007 regulation assigned the Education Authority to evaluate the enrolment procedures of schools to monitor their compliance with the new rules...the Education Authority has only investigated cases on a few occasions and has not exploited its sanctioning power.

propositions.text: 2010 right-wing government reformed public and higher education, centralizing school system and increasing control
propositions.quote: Following the election in 2010 the right-wing government elaborated a concept for the renewal of both the public education and the higher education system...The municipality maintained schools were integrated into a centralised school system, which is maintained by the state.

paragraphs.summary: Court describes 2007 Public Education Act reforms to reduce segregation, 2010 government centralized school system and increased control.

propositions.text: Claimants' fears about education are speculative and insufficiently supported by evidence
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that the claimants' fears with respect to education are speculative, and given the preponderance of the objective evidence, there is insufficient evidence to persuade the panel that the minor claimants would have to return to Grade 1.

propositions.text: Claimants left Hungary 8 years ago; programs now exist to foster education which claimants could use
propositions.quote: Moreover, since the claimants have left Hungary some 8 years ago, programmes at the operational level have been put in place to foster education amongst all children. It would be up to the claimants, to take advantage of those programmes.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes claimants' education fears are speculative; programs exist now to foster education which claimants could use.

propositions.text: Principal claimant testified family home in Hungary was destroyed
propositions.quote: The principal claimant testified that the family home in XXXX has been destroyed.

propositions.text: No objective evidence of home destruction was provided
propositions.quote: There was no objective evidence of that destruction put before the panel.

propositions.text: Evidence could have been obtained since husband is in Hungary
propositions.quote: As the principal claimant's husband is currently in Hungary, the panel finds that this evidence could readily have been obtained.

propositions.text: No nexus shown between alleged destruction and Convention grounds due to lack of reliable evidence
propositions.quote: In any event, the panel is not persuaded that there is a nexus between the alleged destruction of the property, and the Convention definition, because there was no reliable evidence put before the panel about who destroyed the property, or their motive for doing so.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant testified family home destroyed; court finds no objective evidence or nexus to Convention grounds; evidence could have been obtained.

propositions.text: Principal claimant's mother remains in Hungary and no evidence claimants cannot live with her
propositions.quote: As well, the principal claimant's mother remains in Hungary, and there was no evidence placed before the panel that they could not live with her until such time that they could establish their own household.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no evidence claimants cannot live with principal claimant's mother in Hungary until establishing own household.

propositions.text: Federal Court disagreed with Board's state protection findings and returned matter for redetermination
propositions.quote: This matter was returned to the Board for redetermination, because the Federal Court disagreed with the Division's state protection findings...

propositions.text: Principal claimant explained failure to seek state protection due to police not protecting Roma routinely
propositions.quote: In her testimony, the principal claimant explained the failure to seek state protection as being understandable, in a climate where the police do not routinely protect Roma persons.

propositions.text: Principal claimant asserted Federal Court accepted lack of police protection
propositions.quote: She seemed to assert, that even the Federal Court had accepted the lack of police protection in its decision.

paragraphs.summary: Federal Court returned matter for redetermination on state protection; principal claimant explained failure to seek protection due to police climate.

propositions.text: Federal Court found Board lacked analysis on adequate state protection for Roma victims
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the true reasoning behind the decision of the Federal Court lies in its statement at paragraph 15 of the decision. The statement indicates that the Federal Court found the Board had not provided any analysis as to how it reached its conclusion that there is adequate state protection in Hungary for Roma who are victims of crime, police abuse, discrimination, or persecution.

propositions.text: Federal Court rejected Board's conclusions based on contrary documentary evidence
propositions.quote: The Federal Court rejected the Board's conclusions in light of documentary evidence to the contrary.

propositions.text: Federal Court did not accept all Roma are unable to access state protection
propositions.quote: The panel does not read in the Federal Court's statement a blanket acceptance that all Roma are unable to access state protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Federal Court rejected Board's state protection analysis but did not accept all Roma lack access to protection.

propositions.text: Balogh decision supports establishing risk by examining similarly situated individuals, not just personal targeting
propositions.quote: The panel finds persuasive the words of Le Blanc J. in Balogh...persecution can be established by examining the situation of similarly situated individuals...the Balogh decision is consistent with these principles.

propositions.text: Being Roma in Hungary alone is insufficient to establish more than a mere possibility of persecution
propositions.quote: ...the mere fact of being of Roma ethnicity in Hungary is not, in and of itself, sufficient to establish that an applicant faces more than a mere possibility of persecution upon return...

propositions.text: Both subjective and objective fear are components of a valid refugee claim
propositions.quote: Both subjective fear and objective fear are components in respect of a valid claim for refugee status...

propositions.text: Applicant must link general country evidence to specific circumstances to establish claim
propositions.quote: The applicant has a burden of establishing a link between the general documentary evidence and the applicant's specific circumstances...

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Balogh supports risk by similarly situated individuals; being Roma alone insufficient; subjective and objective fear required; applicant must link evidence.

propositions.text: General country conditions do not show all Roma face persecution; panel considered claimants' specific circumstances
propositions.quote: the panel finds that it does not support a conclusion that the general country conditions are such that all Roma in Hungary face discrimination amounting to persecution. Rather...the panel considered the particular claimants' circumstances...

paragraphs.summary: Court finds general conditions do not show all Roma face persecution; considered claimants' specific circumstances.

propositions.text: Principal claimant's testimony is inconsistent, contradictory, speculative and unreliable
propositions.quote: the panel found the principal claimant's testimony to be fraught with inconsistencies, contradictions, and unsupported speculation, such that it is not reliable.

propositions.text: Claimants never sought state protection
propositions.quote: Moreover, by her own admission, at no time did the principal claimant seek to engage the state in an effort to obtain protection.

propositions.text: Insufficient credible evidence to find claimants denied fundamental rights at departure
propositions.quote: Accordingly, the panel concludes that there was insufficient credible evidence upon which to find that the claimants were, at any time, being denied any fundamental rights at the time of their departure.

propositions.text: Claimants have not rebutted presumption of state protection as they did not pursue available avenues
propositions.quote: Moreover, the panel concludes that the claimants have not rebutted the presumption of state protection, given that they did not pursue other avenues that may have been available to them.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds principal claimant's testimony unreliable; claimants never sought protection; insufficient evidence of rights denial; presumption of protection not rebutted.

propositions.text: To rebut presumption of state protection, claimant must provide clear and convincing evidence of state's inability
propositions.quote: To rebut the presumption of state protection, a refugee claimant must provide "clear and convincing" evidence of the state's inability to protect its citizens.

propositions.text: Claimant must persuade Board on balance of probabilities that state protection is inadequate
propositions.quote: A refugee claimant who alleges that state protection is inadequate, must persuade the Board that the evidence establishes that the state protection is, in fact, inadequate...it must also satisfy the Board, on a balance of probabilities, that state protection is inadequate.

propositions.text: State's serious efforts to protect citizens means mere failures do not rebut presumption
propositions.quote: Where a state is in effective control of its territory, has military, police, and civil authority in place, and makes serious efforts to protect its citizens, the mere fact that the state's efforts are not always successful will not rebut the presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: Subjective reluctance to engage state does not rebut presumption in functioning democracy
propositions.quote: A refugee claimant cannot rebut the presumption of state protection, in a functioning democracy, by asserting only a subjective reluctance to engage the state.

propositions.text: Doubting protection effectiveness without testing it does not rebut presumption
propositions.quote: Doubting the effectiveness of the protection offered by the state when one has not really tested it, does not rebut the existence of a presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court states claimant must provide clear, convincing evidence to rebut state protection presumption; mere failures or subjective reluctance insufficient.

propositions.text: Refugee protection is surrogate, invoked after unsuccessful state protection attempts
propositions.quote: Refugee protection is meant to be a form of surrogate protection, to be invoked only in those situations where the refugee claimant has unsuccessfully sought the protection of their home state.

propositions.text: Claimant must approach state for protection when reasonably available
propositions.quote: The onus is on the refugee claimant to approach the state for protection in situations where state protection might be reasonably forthcoming.

propositions.text: Failure to pursue state protection in functioning democracy usually fatal to claim without compelling explanation
propositions.quote: In the absence of a compelling explanation, a failure to pursue state protection opportunities within the home state will usually be fatal to a refugee claim, at least where the state is a functioning democracy with a willingness and the apparatus necessary to provide a measure of protection to its citizens.

paragraphs.summary: Court states refugee protection is surrogate; claimant must seek state protection; failure to do so usually fatal without compelling reason.

propositions.text: Claimant's burden of proof increases with level of democracy in home state
propositions.quote: The refugee claimant's burden of proof is directly proportional to the level of democracy in the state in question: the more democratic the state's institutions, the more the refugee claimant must have done to exhaust all courses of action open to them.

propositions.text: In functioning democracy, claimant has heavy burden to show why domestic remedies were not exhausted
propositions.quote: In a functioning democracy, a refugee claimant will have a heavy burden when attempting to show that they should not have been required to exhaust all of the recourses available to them domestically before claiming refugee status.

paragraphs.summary: Court states claimant's burden increases with democracy level; heavy burden to show why domestic remedies not exhausted.

propositions.text: A refugee claimant must show they took all reasonable steps to seek protection considering country context and interactions with authorities.
propositions.quote: A refugee claimant must show that they have taken all reasonable steps in the circumstances to seek protection, taking into account the context of the country of origin, the steps taken, and the refugee claimant's interactions with the authorities.

propositions.text: Local failures by authorities do not mean state fails to protect unless part of broader pattern of inability or refusal.
propositions.quote: Local failures by authorities to provide protection does not mean that the state, as a whole, fails to protect its citizens, unless the failures form part of a broader pattern of the state's inability, or refusal, to provide protection.

propositions.text: No government must guarantee perfect protection; less than perfect protection is insufficient to justify a claim.
propositions.quote: No government is expected to guarantee perfect protection to all of its citizens at all times, and the fact that a state is not always successful in protecting its citizens is not enough to justify a claim.

propositions.text: Effective control, presence of authorities, and serious efforts to protect citizens indicate less than perfect protection is reasonable.
propositions.quote: Especially where a state is in effective control of its territory, has military, police and civil authorities in place, and is making serious efforts to protect its citizens.

propositions.text: Less than perfect protection does not mean state is unwilling or unable to offer reasonable protection.
propositions.quote: Less than perfect protection is not a basis to determine that a state is either unwilling or unable to offer reasonable protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states refugee claimants must show reasonable steps to seek protection; local failures don't prove state failure unless systemic; less than perfect protection is insufficient to justify claims.

propositions.text: The panel must determine current state protection relevant to the claim.
propositions.quote: The panel is required to determine the state protection provided at the present time that is relevant.

propositions.text: The panel finds protection for Roma in Hungary today is operationally adequate based on its analysis.
propositions.quote: The panel's analysis of the protection available to Roma in Hungary today is such that, protection is operationally adequate based on its analysis that follows.

propositions.text: Panel must consider actual current situation, not just state efforts or plans.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that regard must be given to what is actually happening, and not what the state is endeavouring to put in place.

propositions.text: The panel finds government efforts have translated into adequate operational state protection.
propositions.quote: In this case, the panel finds the government's efforts have "actually translated into adequate state protection" at the operational level.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the panel must assess current state protection and concludes Hungary provides operationally adequate protection to Roma today.

propositions.text: Roma in Hungary face discrimination, violence, and some police inaction with anti-Roma sentiments.
propositions.quote: The panel acknowledges that the Roma minority population in Hungary, experience discrimination in many aspects of their daily lives, and at times, violence and abuse at the hands of some racist elements in Hungary. This includes, the lack of action on the part of some police officers who also demonstrate anti-Roma sentiments.

propositions.text: Human rights NGOs report Roma suffer social and economic exclusion and discrimination in almost all fields.
propositions.quote: The Board's documentary package indicates that "Human rights NGOs continued to report that Roma suffered social and economic exclusion and discrimination in almost all fields of life."

propositions.text: Dissolution of Hungarian Guards and Jobbik's re-casting reduce present danger to claimants.
propositions.quote: However, with the formal dissolution of the Hungarian Guards in 2013, and with the right-wing Jobbik Party re-casting itself as a more inclusive but still nationalist party, the panel is not persuaded that there is a present danger to the claimants.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Roma face discrimination and some police inaction, but recent political changes reduce present danger to claimants.

propositions.text: No current reports of right-wing nationalist marches targeting Roma exist today in Hungary.
propositions.quote: The panel also notes from its reading of the documentary materials... that there are no current reports of right-wing and nationalist marches or gatherings in Hungary that are targeting, harassing, and threatening Roma.

propositions.text: Discriminatory attitudes persist but no evidence that nationalist groups target Roma now or are state-supported.
propositions.quote: While discriminatory attitudes persist among some groups and people in Hungary today, there is no documented evidence before the panel to suggest... that other nationalist or right-wing groups have been targeting Roma today... or that these groups are supported by the State.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no current nationalist targeting of Roma or state support, though discriminatory attitudes persist.

propositions.text: Claimants' counsel argues Hungary's current EU migrant stance shows worsening situation for Roma claimants.
propositions.quote: Counsel for the claimants invited the panel to extrapolate... that, the current situation for the claimants is worse than when they came to Canada. He cites Hungary's position toward migrants as demonstrative of its position towards Roma.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the conclusion that Hungary's migrant stance necessarily worsens Roma situation.
propositions.quote: With respect, the panel cannot draw such a conclusion as an inevitability, as it is not only Hungary that is opposed to the mass migration seen today.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants argue Hungary's migrant stance worsens Roma situation; the court rejects this conclusion.

propositions.text: Police arrest and prosecute perpetrators of crimes against Roma and minorities; recourse is available if dissatisfied.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence indicates, that police arrest and prosecute the perpetrators of crimes, including crimes committed against Roma, and other ethnic minorities and their property... recourse would be available to them.

propositions.text: Organizations assist Roma in accessing government services and protections; panel considered their operational effect.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the documentary evidence indicates, that there are a number of organizations and agencies that assist Hungarians of Romani ethnicity... The panel emphasizes, that it has considered the effect of these programs and initiatives at the operational level, or on the ground.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds police prosecute crimes against Roma and organizations assist Roma in accessing protections, with operational effect considered.

propositions.text: Hungarian authorities have acted against Hungarian Guard Association and seek to ban Civil Guard Association for anti-Roma activities.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the Hungarian authorities have taken action against the Hungarian Guard Association, and have initiated processes for banning the Civil Guard Association, on the grounds that their anti-Roma activities threaten public order.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Hungarian authorities acted against anti-Roma groups threatening public order.

propositions.text: Government prosecutes and punishes officials who commit abuses, including in security services.
propositions.quote: However, the RPD notes, that the government prosecutes and punishes officials who commit abuses, whether in the security services or elsewhere in the government.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the government prosecutes officials who commit abuses, including in security services.

propositions.text: EU FRA report states no specific complaints mechanism for racist police abuse; criminal abuse can be reported to Prosecutorial Investigation Office.
propositions.quote: According to a report on discrimination in Hungary, produced by the European Union's (EU) Agency for Fundamental Rights (FRA)... there is no specific complaints mechanism dealing with racist and related abuse by police officers ... Nevertheless, if victims are subjected to abuses of police power that meet the threshold for criminal liability, they can file a report with the competent Prosecutorial Investigation Office.

propositions.text: Non-criminal police abuses are examined by police unit heads responsible for the staff member.
propositions.quote: Abuses of power by police that are not regarded [as] a violation of fundamental rights are examined and decided upon by the head of [the] unit at the police responsible for the staff member against whom allegations of abuse were made.

paragraphs.summary: The EU FRA report states no specific complaints mechanism for racist police abuse; criminal abuse can be reported to Prosecutorial Investigation Office; non-criminal abuses examined by police unit heads.

propositions.text: Hungarian National Police prioritize educational and employment opportunities for Roma youth via internal instruction and support programs.
propositions.quote: The Hungarian National Police has been treating the educational as well as employment opportunities of the Roma youth as high priority on both strategic and operational levels since the internal instruction No. 1/2010.HNP came into force... Secondary [school] application system can assure [that] supported young Roma get their high school diploma... The higher education application system provides support for [Roma] to complete their college or university studies and then to get employment within the police.

paragraphs.summary: Hungarian National Police prioritize Roma youth education and employment through strategic and operational programs.

propositions.text: Complaints can be brought to police units or IPCB; complaints decided by police unit heads with appeal options; lack of independence may affect effectiveness.
propositions.quote: Sources indicate that complaints can be brought to the relevant police unit or the Independent Police Complaints Board (IPCB)... complaints can be submitted to the responsible police unit within 30 days... complaint is decided on by the head of the relevant police unit... complainant may appeal the "first instance decision"... complaint submitted to the police unit allegedly responsible... cannot be regarded as an independent forum... may have a negative impact on the effectiveness of "ordinary complaint procedures".

propositions.text: IPCB investigates police violations of fundamental rights; complaints must be filed within 20 days, with some extensions; IPCB can forward cases to police if no violation found.
propositions.quote: According to the website of the IPCB, complaints must be filed... within 20 days... If the 20-day deadline has passed, but not 30 days, an individual can file a complaint with "the head of the police office..." The case will be forwarded by the IPCB to the relevant police organ if the board concludes that: - there was no violation of a fundamental right...

paragraphs.summary: Complaints against police can be made to police units or IPCB with appeal rights; IPCB investigates fundamental rights violations but may forward cases back to police.

propositions.text: Government legislation and initiatives produce results; Hungary provides protection for all citizens including Roma.
propositions.quote: The RPD finds that the government has enacted legislation, and put in place many tactical initiatives across several departments and they are producing results on the ground.

propositions.text: Hungary's evolving measures have operational impact; police investigate crimes against Roma and hold perpetrators accountable.
propositions.quote: The RPD finds that the documentary evidence... demonstrates that Hungary continues to provide protection for all its citizens, including Roma and other ethnic minorities... police do investigate crimes against Roma, and that perpetrators are being held responsible when there is sufficient evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Hungary's legislation and initiatives produce results, providing protection and police accountability for Roma.

propositions.text: The key question is whether adequate state protection exists at the operational level for these claimants.
propositions.quote: In the final analysis, the question to be answered is if there is adequate state protection, at the operational level, for these particular claimants.

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies the issue as whether adequate operational state protection exists for these claimants.

propositions.text: Police oversight agencies play an important role in demonstrating adequate state protection and ensuring police accountability.
propositions.quote: More substantively, suggesting that police oversight agencies have no role in demonstrating adequate state protection is like saying senior policing management has no role in policing due to their oversight function... The transparency and accompanying public criticism of the state protection apparatus is an important ingredient to reforms and improvement in protection services accorded to Roma citizens.

propositions.text: Effective policing deters crime by arresting and prosecuting wrongdoers and publicizing convictions.
propositions.quote: Effective policing can have a deterrent effect by arresting and successfully prosecuting wrongdoers accompanied by the declaratory publicity attached to successful convictions.

propositions.text: Victims must report crimes and cooperate with police and oversight agencies to ensure effective crime prevention and protection.
propositions.quote: No crime prevention process can be effective if victims of crime do not report incidents to the police and proactively cooperate in their investigations, including complaining if not satisfied with the efforts of the police.

propositions.text: Access to police oversight agencies improves protection for Roma against random crimes over time.
propositions.quote: The requirement to access police oversight agencies is particularly important where the persecution is in the form of random incidents... I would argue, yes it would.

paragraphs.summary: A prior court explains police oversight agencies are vital for adequate protection, deterrence, and crime prevention, especially for Roma victims.

propositions.text: Claimants bear the burden to prove state unwillingness or inability to provide protection with clear and convincing evidence.
propositions.quote: The RPD concludes, that as stated above, the burden is on the claimants to provide clear and convincing evidence that the state is either unwilling, or unable, to provide them with adequate protection.

propositions.text: Claimants must rebut presumption of state protection on balance of probabilities; RPD does not provide that proof.
propositions.quote: It is not for the RPD to provide that proof, rather it is the claimant who bears the legal burden, of rebutting the presumption that state protection exists by adducing clear and convincing evidence which satisfies the panel, on a balance of probabilities.

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimants must prove state unwillingness or inability to protect with clear and convincing evidence, rebutting presumption of protection.

propositions.text: Claimants have not rebutted presumption of state protection and made no effort to obtain it.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes, after careful consideration of all of the evidence, that the claimants have not rebutted the presumption of state protection. Indeed, they made no effort to obtain it.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimants failed to rebut presumption of state protection and made no effort to seek it.

propositions.text: The panel is guided by X (Re) 2017 CANLII 144421 (CA CISR) which found state protection available to claimants.
propositions.quote: The panel is further guided by the recent decision X (Re) 2017 CANLII 144421 (CA CISR), in which it was determined that state protection was available to the claimants.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes guidance from a recent decision finding state protection available to claimants.

propositions.text: Federal Court found RPD reasonably considered Hungarian legislative measures and operational effectiveness.
propositions.quote: The RPD is further guided by the recent Federal Court decision in which Justice Boswell found, that the RPD reasonably considered the legislative measures taken by the Hungarian government, and their operational effectiveness: The RPD reasonably concluded that the Applicants had not provided sufficient evidence either to rebut the presumption of adequate state protection in Budapest or to show that relocating to Budapest would be unreasonable in view of the Applicants' particular situation and circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Federal Court found RPD reasonably considered Hungarian measures and operational effectiveness in protection assessment.

propositions.text: State protection would be reasonably forthcoming to claimants if they diligently sought it upon return to Hungary.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that state protection would be reasonably forthcoming to these claimants, in their particular situation and circumstances, if they required it and were to diligently seek it, upon return to Hungary.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes state protection would be reasonably available to claimants if diligently sought upon return.

propositions.text: Claimants have not established serious possibility of persecution or risk of cruel treatment, torture, or danger upon return to Hungary.
propositions.quote: The RPD concludes that in the particular circumstances of these claimants, the claimants have not established a serious possibility of persecution, or that they would, on a balance of probabilities, be personally subjected to a risk to life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, or to a danger of torture upon return to Hungary.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimants have not shown serious risk of persecution or cruel treatment upon return to Hungary.

propositions.text: These claims are rejected.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, these claims are rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects these claims.
